chunks: And when we said that what is like a cause for disbelief does not necessarily be disbelief in the moment, if one believed in the Capable among us regarding a power that it is valid for Him to do a new act in other bodies, that would be an error and ignorance, not disbelief, and it is not impossible that it is known from the state of this believer that if a prophet appeared calling to his prophethood and made a miracle that Allah Almighty would perform through his hand an act such that the causes of humans do not reach it, that he would not accept it, and this inevitably if he knew it were a miracle he would have accepted it, and what preceded of his belief in the capability of the Capable was like a cause for this, and it did not necessitate that it follows its course in disbelief.
ai.seo_question: Is believing in the Imam's ability to perform miracles considered disbelief in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi distinguishes between mere error (ghalat) and disbelief (kufr), arguing that believing the Imam possesses the power to perform miracles is a foundational premise rather than a definitive rejection of truth. This preliminary belief acts as a causal precursor (sabab) to acceptance; once the miracle is verified as divine and beyond human capability, the individual's prior stance facilitates their recognition of the Imam's authority without requiring a complete overhaul of their theological framework.
